newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal school blast kills one, injures five.
newsitem.headline: Portugal school blast kills one, injures five.

text.p: A woman was killed and five people were injured in an explosion at a Portuguese school on Friday which fire brigade and local government officials said had been caused by a bomb.
There were no children amongst the victims of the blast which occurred at around 0815 GMT at a primary school in the small town of Fundao in central Portugal, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Lisbon.
Fire brigade and local government officials at the scene were in doubt about the cause of the explosion, although police bomb squad experts were still examining the site.
Fundao town councillor Jose Soares told local TSF radio that the explosion, which did extensive damage to the ground floor of the school, had been caused by an "explosive device."
A senior fire brigade official told the Lusa news agency that the device had been placed against the outside wall of the building.
There was no immediate indication of the motive nor of who might be responsible for the blast at the school which was semi-deserted at the time.
Portuguese schools have not yet reopened after the long summer holiday.
Education Minister Marcal Grilo visited the scene and said afterwards that he was "enormously worried" by the incident.
The dead woman, named as Ana Maria Nunes, 32, and the injured were all employed at the school, police said.
Three of the injured were in serious condition and were being treated in nearby hospitals. The other two people suffered only slight injuries.
